data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Ita was the goddess of the healing waters. Her name derives from the Latin word 'ita', meaning 'self' or 'same'. In Christianity, Ita may symbolize divine healing and renewal. The name Ita carries the meaning “Goddess of the Healing Waters” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ita usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the healing waters and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Ita belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the Healing Waters.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ita total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: איטה
in_hebrew.meaning: איטה משמעת נאמנות לאלוקים ולבניית הבית
in_hebrew.long_meaning: איטה הוא שם שמקורו בשפה העברית ומשמעותו היא נאמנות לאלוקים ולבניית הבית. השם איטה מורכב מהשורש אמן שמשמעותו נאמנות וביטחון. השם איטה הוא שם נדיר אך משמעותו עמוקה ומרמזת על קשר חזק עם האל ובניית הבית הרוחני.

in_greek.name: Ίτα
in_greek.meaning: Η Ίτα σημαίνει πιστότητα και αφοσίωση
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Ίτα είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα και σημαίνει πιστότητα και αφοσίωση. Το όνομα Ίτα έχει σχέση με την ελληνική λέξη 'αἰτία' που σημαίνει 'αίτιο' ή 'λόγος', αλλά και με την έννοια της πιστότητας και της αφοσίωσης. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, η έννοια της πιστότητας και της αφοσίωσης είναι πολύ σημαντική.

in_latin.name: Ita
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Ita is derived from Latin and means faithful and devoted. The etymology of Ita is linked to the Latin word 'ita' which means 'so' or 'thus', but in the context of names, it signifies faithfulness and loyalty. In early Christian tradition, the concept of faithfulness and devotion to God was highly valued.

historical_references.reference: Ita Altar - An altar dedicated to the Virgin Mary, known as the Ita Altar, was discovered in 1609 in the ancient Mayan ruins of Tulum, Mexico. The altar was adorned with European-style symbols, suggesting that it was used by a Christianized Mayan community. This is an important reminder of the syncretic nature of Christianity in the Americas, where indigenous beliefs were often blended with European ones.

Ita Peña - Ita Peña was a 16th-century Franciscan priest who played a significant role in the evangelization of the Guatemalan highlands. He is known for his work in translating the Bible into the Quiché language and for his efforts to convert the indigenous population. Ita Peña's work helped to establish a strong Christian presence in the region and contributed to the spread of the faith throughout Central America.
